evidence: Source review of the final staging-to-sweep merge against native build 1 Swift sources. Ticket detail still emits record_sha256; backlog/resume accept the older extra fingerprint without a stale-write requirement. Chief, Manager, Ticket conversation, review approval, recap, resource-version and notification device contracts retain native-required fields. Native approval choices are owner/Manager/Chief, so removal of Ticket approval holders does not change these choices. Removed Feedback and Scheduled features now return HTTP 404; FeedbackModel and SettingsView catch the error and show retry/error state in those sections. These sections do not work against the sweep, by the approved removal. Goal conversation send/reset/start routes remain retired as in the staging review; historical transcripts remain readable by conversation id and the optional goal conversationId decodes nil. The app handles ios_update_required centrally and retains drafts in its local outbox; the build middleware remains unchanged. Build floor stays 1 for retained features. This is source compatibility evidence only: no signed device, TestFlight, native reconnect, live action, or draft survival scenario ran in this ticket. CI runtime checks remain separate evidence. CI repair review: the baseline tuple annotation changes no runtime behavior. Paused startup permits GET/HEAD of only the deployment-status resource body. Native deployment-status and health paths remain unchanged. Packaging repair only changes native offline probe paths and pins the direct Codex CLI. It changes no native-facing HTTP contract. Manager manual-value authorization now resides at shared command intake, with the same staging page/held-goal capability. This restores the capability without response-shape changes. Manager page read repair: both central admission lists now apply the existing rank rule. HTTP tests prove that owner reads retain HTTP 200, identical page output, and successful readings. The change refuses agent reads without the required rank. Owner response shapes stay unchanged. The native APIClient does not set Worker actor headers. Build floor remains 1. No signed-device checks ran for this change. Combined staging merge review: Source review of the launch-parent recheck keeps native build 1 compatible. The only backend edits are in src/planner/server_lifecycle: logic/shutdown.py adds two pure policy helpers, supervisor.py rechecks an unverified launch parent when SIGINT or SIGTERM arrives, and process_identity.py prints why a busctl check failed. These run only in the local supervisor process that owns the server's lifetime. No server route, serializer, payload shape or contract changes, and no Swift source references server_lifecycle. Prior review (pre-Mac pin adoption fix) stands for everything else. The other incoming changes affect deployment tooling, test infrastructure, and web rail behavior. They add no native-facing routes or payload changes. This combined review retains both source reviews and build floor 1. No signed-device checks ran. Expected staging PR #588 merge review: the Chief chose to retain the sweep owner-update protocol and omit PR #586 legacy recovery. update_requests.py, update_runner.py and deploy.yml retain the sweep side. The backend source is identical to the prior reviewed sweep candidate, so native retained routes and payloads remain unchanged. Incoming recovery tests and documentation do not change native HTTP contracts. Minimum native build remains 1. No signed-device checks ran. The scratch install-path proof is separate and is not yet complete. Combined with staging 82ee67f50 (uncompressed Mac update channel): the two changes touch separate backend files, and that change's own review stands. Mac project workspace review (t_b9d7uht3), merged with staging 221749ee5: native build 1 stays compatible and the minimum remains 1. Hook messages that Claude now sends produce no conversation record rows or view fields, and the adapter already ignores their session ids. Command reply review (t_6cx9cyn2): native build 1 stays compatible and the minimum remains 1. The conversation view gains one row kind, command_reply, with body {kind, reply_text}. No route, request body or existing field changed. Swift ConversationBody decodes kind as a plain String and every other field as optional, so a command_reply body decodes with empty text, and ConversationModel skips rows with empty text. An old app therefore shows nothing for the new row, which is the same as before this change. latestMessage lists only agent_message, user_input and permission_ask kinds, so the preview line is unchanged. VIEW_PROJECTION_VERSION stays 4. The executor protocol goes from 20 to 21 for the Mac wire, and no Swift source reads an executor route (grep of ios/). No signed-device checks ran. Skill delete and file-write review (t_j22a7wex): native build 1 stays compatible and the minimum remains 1. The change adds two owner-only routes, DELETE /api/skills/<name> and PUT /api/skills/<name>/files, and no Swift source calls either (grep of ios/). No existing route, request body or response shape changed. The app reads GET /api/skills and shows panels-manager and panels-worker, and the Chief screen reads panels-chief-of-staff. Delete refuses those role skills, so the app always finds them. A Worker type's specialist skill cannot be deleted while the type names it, and SettingsView already treats that lookup as optional. Startup provisioning now prunes dead links in agent homes, which no native client sees. No signed-device checks ran. Worker-type delete and per-Ticket guide review (t_uj1kg9pa): native build 1 stays compatible and the minimum remains 1. The change adds the owner-only DELETE /api/worker-types/<type>, which no Swift source calls (grep of ios/). The Ticket screen (TicketView.load) and Review decision (ReviewDecision) use the Ticket's own workflow from GET /api/tickets?detail=full, and fetch /api/worker-types/<type>/manifest only when that workflow is absent. tickets/views.py always emits workflow from the Ticket's saved copy, so a Ticket whose type was deleted still loads and reviews on device. A unit test proves that this detail read returns HTTP 200 with the Ticket's own stages after its type is deleted. POST /api/worker-types drops the always-empty migrations key, and GET /api/tickets/<id>/worker-self drops worker and worker_skill_path. No Swift source reads either route (grep of ios/). The board's column order still comes from Coding, now through a named constant, with an unchanged response shape. The other changes are server-to-agent text: the worker step opener, the memory-loss notice and the conversation-start role text. The app never reads that text. SettingsView lists /api/workers and treats the specialist skill lookup as optional, so a deleted type simply leaves the list. No route the app calls changes its request body or response fields. No signed-device checks ran. Mac link freeze review (t_9ftm3bc1): native build 1 stays compatible and the minimum remains 1. The changes are in the Mac executor link, the Mac inbox save path, conversation storage retry, and a new local event-loop task listing socket. The new error codes retry_later and save_failed are sent only on the executor WebSocket and in Mac outbox receipts, which no Swift source reads (grep of ios/ for executor routes and both codes finds none). APIClient decodes error.code as a plain String, so an unknown code would not break decoding in any case. The conversation read GET /api/conversation/conversations/{id} no longer waits on the conversation lock, with the same response fields. VPS-only conversation writes now retry instead of parking, which changes timing only. The executor protocol version stays 21, and the new panels server-event-loop-tasks command uses a local Unix socket that no native client sees. No route, request body or response shape changed. No signed-device checks ran. Out-of-date conversation view rebuild review (t_3pm5qzcn): native build 1 stays compatible and the minimum remains 1. After startup the server rebuilds stored conversation views whose projection version is old, in the background. Until a view is rebuilt, GET /view, /view/tail and /view/receipts answer HTTP 409 with detail 'Conversation view is upgrading' instead of HTTP 500 or a broken stream. No route, request body or response field changed, and VIEW_PROJECTION_VERSION stays 4. APIClient.validate throws APIError for any non-2xx status, so the app treats the 409 as a failed read. ConversationNavigation's tail loop sets model.error and reconnects after 2 s, and the snapshot frame that follows the rebuild clears the error and shows the transcript. ConversationModel.refreshSnapshot and the receipts read in applyTail handle the error the same way. While a view waits, the app shows 'Server returned HTTP 409.', because the body carries detail and not error.message. Before this change it showed a failure for the same conversations, so nothing gets worse. No signed-device checks ran.
